The previous 583 was read off the implementation rather than measured while running it; measured on the released implementation: 256 bytes per scanned index entry at both 32,000 and 128,000 tokens. The previous 68 was read off the implementation rather than measured while running it; index scanning is NOT gated by a threshold: the zero index scans that suggested one were an instrumentation gap in tools/run_deepseek_v4_reference_oracle.py, whose --measure-kv wrapped Attention.forward but left Indexer.forward unwrapped, so an untiled rung counted none. Re-measured with the indexer instrumented, the released implementation scans its index at every context tested: 5,250 (layer, position) index pairs at 1,000 tokens and 42,000 at 8,000, i.e. 21 csa layers x ceil(context/4) compressed entries, exactly as the unconditional model says. With the threshold at 8,001 the profile under-predicted the measured rungs by 1.12x at 1,000 tokens and 1.60x at 8,000; at 0 it matches all five measured rungs to within 0.4%. index_scan_threshold.corrected_measurement: Re-instrumented, the index is scanned at every rung and the count is exactly context/4 throughout: 250, 2,000, 8,000, 32,000 and 50,000 entries per csa layer at 1,001 / 8,001 / 32,001 / 128,001 / 200,001 tokens. index_scan_min_compressed_entries is back to 0, which is the unconditional scan the profile always had.
index_scan_threshold.effect_on_published_numbers: None. The threshold only ever bit below ~8,001 compressed entries, far under the 200,000 and 1,000,000 contexts this program makes claims at. The roofline studies were re-run against both states and every headline number is byte-identical.
index_scan_threshold.lesson: A measurement that disagrees with a model is evidence about one of them, and which one is not decided by whichever is easier to change. Here the model was right and the instrument was incomplete -- and the tell was available at the time: a threshold that happened to fall exactly between the tiled and untiled rungs is a suspicious coincidence, and nobody asked why.
index_scan_threshold.what_was_claimed: That the released implementation scans no sparse index below ~8,001 compressed entries, recorded in commit 98f2965 as index_scan_min_compressed_entries = 8001.
index_scan_threshold.why_it_was_wrong: An instrumentation gap, not a behaviour. The oracle's --measure-kv wrapped Attention.forward but left Indexer.forward unwrapped, so a rung that did not tile its prefill recorded no index reads at all. The 1,001 and 8,001 rungs were untiled and reported zero; the longer rungs tiled and went through the wrapped path. The threshold was the boundary of the instrumentation, not of the model.

kv_entry_measurement.note: The structure of the profile was already correct and is unchanged: csa reads top_k + window main entries and scans context/4 index entries, hca reads context/128 + window, window reads 128. Only the two per-entry byte sizes were wrong. A deployment that chose an FP8 KV latent would read 512 bytes rather than 1,024; that is a design choice and must then be applied to both sides of any comparison, so it is not assumed here.
